title: Settlement of Reykjavík
description: Ingólfur Arnarson, by tradition the first permanent Norse settler, makes his home at Reykjavík.

title: Althing founded
description: Chieftains set up a general assembly for the whole island, one of the oldest parliaments in the world.

title: Christianity adopted
description: The Althing accepts the lawspeaker's ruling that all Icelanders shall be baptised, avoiding a civil war.

title: Bishopric of Skálholt
description: Ísleifur Gissurarson is consecrated the first bishop of Iceland, with his seat at Skálholt.

title: Snorri Sturluson killed
description: The chieftain and author of the Prose Edda and Heimskringla is killed at his home on the orders of the Norwegian king.

title: Old Covenant
description: After decades of feuding the chieftains swear allegiance to the King of Norway, ending the independent commonwealth.

title: Black Death reaches Iceland
place: Hvalfjörður (where the plague ship is said to have landed)
description: A ship brings the plague to Iceland, where it kills perhaps half the population.

title: Execution of Jón Arason
description: The last Catholic bishop in Iceland is beheaded with two of his sons, completing the Lutheran Reformation.

title: Guðbrand's Bible
description: Bishop Guðbrandur Þorláksson prints the first complete Bible in Icelandic, helping to keep the written language unchanged.

title: Danish trade monopoly
description: The Danish king reserves all trade with Iceland for merchants of a few Danish towns, a system that lasts until 1786.

title: Turkish Abductions
description: Barbary corsairs raid the coast and carry off about 400 people to be sold as slaves in North Africa.

title: Laki eruption
description: An eight-month fissure eruption poisons the land, and the famine that follows kills about a fifth of the population.

title: Reykjavík chartered
description: Reykjavík, then a small village, is given a town charter and trading rights.

title: Althing restored
description: The Althing, abolished in 1800, meets again in Reykjavík as an advisory assembly.

title: Constitution of 1874
description: King Christian IX grants Iceland a constitution giving the Althing power to make laws on domestic matters.

title: Home rule
description: Hannes Hafstein takes office as the first Minister for Iceland resident in Reykjavík and answerable to the Althing.

title: Act of Union
description: Iceland becomes a sovereign kingdom sharing only its king with Denmark.

title: British occupation
description: British marines land in neutral Iceland to keep it out of German hands, and American forces take over the following year.

title: Republic founded
description: After a referendum Iceland ends the union with Denmark and proclaims a republic at the old assembly site.

title: First Cod War
description: Iceland extends its fishing limit to twelve nautical miles, starting the first of three confrontations with Britain that Iceland wins.

title: Eruption on Heimaey
description: A fissure opens at the edge of the town, the island's people are evacuated overnight and lava buries part of the town.

title: Women's strike
description: About nine in ten Icelandic women stop paid and unpaid work for a day to show their part in the economy.

title: Vigdís Finnbogadóttir elected president
description: Vigdís Finnbogadóttir becomes the first woman in the world to be elected head of state in a national election.

title: Reykjavík Summit
description: Ronald Reagan and Mikhail Gorbachev meet and come close to agreeing to abolish nuclear weapons, opening the way to later arms treaties.

title: Banking collapse
description: The three largest banks fail within days and are taken over by the state, the largest banking collapse relative to the size of an economy.

title: Eyjafjallajökull eruption
description: An eruption under the ice cap sends up an ash cloud that closes most European airspace for several days.
